aggregation: As the TC0-A and TC1 gates (TC0-GATE, 02 §14): any required row FAIL -> FAIL; else any BLOCKED -> BLOCKED; else any UNKNOWN -> UNKNOWN; else PASS. A mutant caught by no property, or a flagged equivalent control, is FAIL; a truncated exploration is never PASS. An evaluator error or a check that does not report is UNKNOWN. Every row's reasons are reported whatever the aggregate.
scope: Accepted-job bounded exploration at 2 tenants, 2 keys, 2 payload digests; per schedule at most 3 submits, 2 deliveries, 2 responses and 1 crash; state cap 2,000,000 (the default of harness/run-service-explore.sh and harness/run-service-fenrir.sh). not_covered: The correspondence between the Shen model and the Rocq A0 model (by reading, not proved) and any proof of the properties: everything here is bounded exploration at the stated scope (2 tenants, 2 keys, 2 digests, small budgets), not a proof and not an unbounded refinement claim. The mutants and their predictions are written by the same author lineage as the model; the equivalent control shows only that the monitor does not flag one behaviour-preserving variant. The handler runs on the draft TC1-D1 durable effects (spec/tc1/DURABLE.md: owner choices unconfirmed, capabilities forgeable), so wrong-tenant is caught dynamically, not refused. The host is the A1 store under the stated storage contract (HANDLER.md section 3, owner choices in section 6 unconfirmed), not a real database (stage A3). The Solo5 row covers the distinct runs of the handler under quick mode (one replay per tape, no hostile-host or tape-negative tests); the full guest checks are the optional TC1 row durable-guest, which does not run the handler. Progress holds only under the stated delivery-fairness and availability assumptions. The contract is not part of slice TC1, and a pass of this gate says nothing about it. Stage A3 (host/service: SQLite under an OTP supervisor, the handler as a Solo5 worker) is covered only by the optional row a3-host-quick, in quick mode: observed history accepted over a bounded crash campaign, not a proof; power loss and fsync are not simulated, so the sync_off mutant is not detected; SQLite, OTP and the tender are trusted; one request per boot over a finite request domain; the host contract is a draft (ledger row SERVICE-A3-HOST). The a3-host-quick row now also carries the stage A4 host families (the upgrade_* campaigns, ten A4 host mutants, 13 history negative tests) with the same limits. Stage A4 (the versioned service upgrade, spec/service/UPGRADE.md) is covered only by the optional rows a4-model, a4-fenrir-refinement, a4-solo5-agreement and a4-retained-replay (ledger row SERVICE-A4-UPGRADE): bounded scope (1 key, at most 2 submits, 1 crash, 1 dispatched run, 4 upgrade steps), not a proof; the model, its mutants and the host families are of one author lineage; the choices of UPGRADE.md section 11 are unconfirmed by the owner; there is no rollback after migrate; the fencing of a stale v1 submit in the real stack rests on a column-count accident (as the A4 author reported; not re-derived by this gate); fsync and power-loss honesty of the upgrade are not tested.
